logline: On graduation day a girl cuts the boyfriend who sold his car to pay her tuition out of her photos and dumps him ('You don't fit where I'm going'); three years later her new boyfriend's big investor turns out to be Nate, she begs to come back, he invites her to his office - and springs the trap with her boyfriend sitting at the table.

hook.mechanic: Cold open on a public snub: a photographer asks 'Boyfriend in the picture too?' and she says 'No, just me' while the boyfriend stands right there holding her flowers; a friend instantly exposes that he paid for her school, she hisses 'Can you not tell people that?' and he answers 'Seriously?' in a close-up. Betrayal plus a secret debt in under 6 s, no setup.
hook.first_line: Boyfriend in the picture too? / No, just me.

beats.summary: HOOK: graduation photo. Photographer: 'Boyfriend in the picture too?' She: 'No, just me.' Friend: 'Wait, didn't he pay for your school?' She: 'Can you not tell people that?' Nate, holding flowers: 'Seriously?'

Flashback '2 YEARS AGO...': he hands over his car keys, watches the car drive off at sunset, phone shows 'Tuition Paid' with $0.50 left; in the kitchen she finds out ('You really did this?'), he says 'You said this was your dream... When I make it, we make it.' She hugs him.
White flash back to graduation day: a hug, then she says 'You don't fit where I'm going.' He: 'After everything?' He walks away through the crowd with the flowers.

Reversal: at a sunset penthouse party her new boyfriend greets 'Mr. Nate', his investor. She: 'You know him?' Nate, in a suit, LV cap and gold glasses: 'We'll talk tomorrow, of course.' and walks past her.

Balcony at night: 'I made the wrong choice... He can't give me the life I thought he could. I should have chose you.' Nate stares, then, walking off: 'Come to my office tomorrow.' She smiles - she thinks she won.
Payoff: she runs into his office and hugs him ('You meant it. So it was true.'); the camera pulls back to reveal her boyfriend sitting at the boardroom table. 'You set me up?'
Real-life tag: rapid live-action handheld flexes (supercars, watch, yacht, jet, designer boxes) under 'MONEY >'.

transcription: faster-whisper 'small' (CPU, int8), word timestamps; every line cross-checked against the burned-in word-by-word captions (they match word for word). Speakers assigned by mouth movement and staging.
why_it_works: The hook is a public humiliation with a twist of debt: she erases him from the photo while he holds her flowers, and a bystander says the quiet part ('didn't he pay for your school?') - the viewer is angry by second 3.
Nate under-reacts ('Seriously?', small face, no shouting) - restraint makes him sympathetic and sets up the cold revenge.

The flashback is told almost without words in three 0.3-0.5 s inserts (keys handed over, car driving off, phone showing 'Tuition Paid' and $0.50) - concrete props carry the sacrifice faster than dialogue could.
The title line 'When I make it, we make it' is planted in the tender flashback, so the breakup line 'You don't fit where I'm going' lands as a direct betrayal of it.

The reversal uses status cues, not exposition: same girl, new rich boyfriend, sunset penthouse - and the boyfriend calls Nate 'Mr. Nate' and 'the investor'. Wardrobe does the rest (suit, monogram cap, gold glasses, NATE pendant).

Two fake-outs build the ending: she confesses and he seems to soften ('Come to my office tomorrow'), she smiles - then the pull-back reveals the boyfriend in the room. The payoff is a camera move, not a line.
Nate's power is shown by stillness: static close-ups, slow blink, walking away mid-scene while she stays in frame reacting.
Lighting tells time and mood: golden-hour graduation, warm dark kitchen for the memory, sunset penthouse for the reversal, blue-hour balcony for the confession, bright cool office for the trap.
Dense, fast dialogue (24 lines in 36 s) with word-by-word captions keeps it readable on mute and leaves no slack.
The live-action 'real me' flex tag with a bass drop turns the fable into the creator's own success story and loops the viewer back to the start.
undetermined: Music track not identified; music notes come from loudness/frequency analysis only (no listening). Tempo ~136 BPM is an estimate.
Photographer as speaker of 'Boyfriend in the picture too?' is inferred (he is the one with the camera; his mouth is not clearly visible).

Continuity: the girl wears a black gown in the opening but a sparkly blue slip dress in the second graduation scene (12.55-15.20), and the graduates' gowns change from black to purple/blue. Treated as the same graduation day; it may be an AI continuity slip.
The office set-up ('You set me up?') is not explained on screen - it is implied the boyfriend's investment meeting is the trap.

Trading/finance relevance: there are NO trading screens, charts or market apps in this reel. The only screen is a full-frame phone payments UI ('Tuition Paid', '$0.50', gibberish text) at 7.30-7.73. Phones appear as props only (she holds hers in the kitchen); 'finance' is carried by status props (suit, office, 'investor').
The live-action tag cuts are very short (0.1-0.2 s) and several are hidden in whip blur; 13 shots is a careful count but may be off by one.

tag.description: Live-action 'real me' flex tag, 13 handheld phone shots in 3.3 s (median ~0.13 s), many joined by motion-blur whips: car selfie with a girl in the next car's window, walk toward red supercars in a garage, diamond watch over purple LED light, Rolls-Royce-style rear seat with starlight headliner, purple-lit van lounge, yacht deck, jet-ski POV at sunset, pool, designer shopping boxes from a car boot, yacht at night, sneaker/clothes room, private jet with black cars, selfie with friends. Constant yellow caption 'MONEY >' plus a small animated pixel-art pickaxe sticker [do not copy]. Music jumps ~5 dB louder with heavy sub-bass here.

sound: Dialogue-led (no narrator V.O.): 24 lines, fast and close-miked, typical AI voices; lines butt against each other with almost no pauses.
A music bed runs under everything at a steady level (RMS about -13 to -16 dB all through the story); a beat track at roughly 136 BPM by onset analysis (estimate). Track not identified.

Low-frequency impact/boom hits land on the time jumps: the cut into the '2 YEARS AGO' flashback (6.5 s), the white flash back to the present (12.0 s), the '3 YEARS LATER' card (15.5-16.5 s) and the hug/reveal in the office (34.5 s) - sub-bass energy rises 10-25 dB at those moments.
At the live-action tag (36.35 s) the music drops in harder: about +5 dB overall and the sub-bass jumps ~15 dB, a bass-heavy drop that sells the flex montage.
method: Auto cut list (frame-difference) checked with 0.1 s frame strips over the whole reel and per-frame difference around doubtful cuts. 54 auto shots -> 40: merged false cuts from a tiny reframe (3.58), a white flash and a bouquet swinging through frame (11.87, 12.27, 12.33), photographers' camera flashes (12.70, 12.88, 13.07, 14.70), talking-head motion (13.78, 13.87, 14.08), and motion blur in the live-action tag (36.80, 37.10, 38.00 folded in as a whip). No missed cuts found; the 3.87 s balcony shot and the 2.47 s tracking shot are single continuous shots.
